title: Conduction through a pipe wall
model: a steel pipe (k 53.33 W/(m K)), bore 10 mm at 100 C, outside 20 mm cooled at 25 W/(m^2 K) to 20 C, 40 mm long, ends insulated; 2.5 mm elements

heat_w.source: steady radial conduction in series with a film: Q = 2 pi L (T_i - T_inf) / (ln(r_o/r_i)/k + 1/(h r_o)) (Incropera & DeWitt, Fundamentals of Heat and Mass Transfer, ch. 3, the cylindrical wall)
heat_w.reason: the temperature, ln r through the wall, is smooth and a quadratic follows it to 1e-5 at 2.5 mm; the film is a boundary integral the quadratic facets of a curved face carry to their area's error, about 1e-4
